chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: The Silas Green show and Bessie Smith
summary: The Silas Green From New Orleans tent show, which his father traveled with, had its own train cars and featured Bessie Smith.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Also, the Silas Green Show, which my father came to Jackson with the first time I saw him, when I was twelve years old... He was with Silas Green, and they had a fantastic show. Bessie Smith was with the show. In fact, she was with that show when she died.
Silas Green From New Orleans, they called it. But it was a great, great traveling tent show.

Well, Silas Green... I didn't know who Silas Green really was. Because the Collier Family owned the show at the time. Evidently, he had been some legend of some kind, but it was called... The show was named Silas Green From New Orleans. Oh, they had some production, production like you just don't see any more.

It was like a... There was a big tent, you know, and they had to bring the chairs. They had their own equipment. In fact, they traveled...they had their own train cars that they traveled in; their own cars on the... They were really first-class. They were about the finest minstrel show out there, other than maybe the Leon Claxton and the Royal American Revue show that used to travel... They had a whole big circus, everything that traveled with that show. And he had spectacular revues, Leon Claxton. In fact, the band that I worked with left home to go with them, and I couldn't go -- you know, to go to Florida to work with the Royal American Revue.
